subject: tiny envelopes
body: I take back everything I said about tiny envelopes being easy. There are now seeds in my keyboard. Can we use the bigger ones for the beans? promise I'll keep the peas out of the printer.
why: SPEC §5.7: situational and self-directed humour contains no insult about another person or company.

subject: boxes
body: Two deep ones. no lids needed ta
why: SPEC §5: a storage-box quantity and specification are ordinary work logistics.

subject: Re: bells for the display
body:
Settled on yellow! sorry for the epic thread over a bell.
> Would red show up on the shelf?
> The backing card is red already.
>> Blue maybe?
>> Blue is nice but the sample is quite dark.
>>> Do you still have yellow?
>>> Yes, there are two finishes.
>>>> Is the matt one easier to photograph?
>>>> It doesn't reflect the ceiling lights.
>>>>> Let's try that against the card.
>>>>> It looks clear from across the shop.
why: SPEC §5: the full quoted history is ordinary colour and display discussion, without sensitive details.

subject: Fwd: matinee club
body:
Could be useful for the noticeboard, see below.

Forwarded newsletter from Brackenfoil Picture House
Our autumn matinee club starts next week. Each screening will have a short introduction about the sets and costumes. The foyer cafe will open before the film. Programmes are available at the ticket desk and everyone is welcome to collect one.
You can ask the desk to remove you from this mailing list.
why: SPEC §5: public cinema programming and noticeboard correspondence do not disclose sensitive information.

subject: soggy bunting update
body: This weather is doing my head in. The bunting is still drying across the spare tables, so I'll bring it tomorrow instead. Colours haven't run, thankfully. what a week.
why: SPEC §5.7: frustration is about weather; equipment condition and return timing are ordinary.

subject: Strings arrived
body:
The strings arrived this morning, thanks. The outer wrapping was torn but the packets inside are all intact. I'll let you know when the instrument is ready to collect.
Tavi Norrin
Oxbriar instrument desk
Replies sent after closing may be read the next working day.
why: SPEC §5: parcel condition, repair scheduling and an opening-hours signature contain no sensitive disclosure.

subject: the hat situation
body: You were right about the wide brim. I now look like a walking lampshade, but at least it fits over the veil. Can we borrow the spare stand for the demonstration too?
why: SPEC §5.7: self-directed clothing humour and an equipment request are not disparagement of a person or company.

subject: label
body: lower left, not centre. looks better there
why: SPEC §5: a brief label-position instruction is ordinary design feedback.

subject: demo table
body: That was a cracking demo, still got the riff stuck in my head. We've found the missing extension lead; it was hiding under the table skirt like a very boring snake. Drop by any time tomorrow and we'll hand it over.
why: SPEC §5.7: enthusiasm and a joke about an inanimate cable insult nobody; the rest is a return arrangement.

subject: Fwd: poems at the stop
body:
Here's the scheme I was trying to describe yesterday.

Press release — Silverfrond Arts Circle
Short poems will appear in the east-side bus shelters this winter. The project pairs local writing groups with volunteer printmakers. Each panel will carry a large-print version and an illustration. The first panels go up after the shelters have been cleaned.
End of public release.
why: SPEC §5: an invented public arts announcement is ordinary outside correspondence.

subject: Re: blue counters
body:
Found them in the little cloth bag. all sorted, no need to send extras.
> Are you missing the blue counters?
> We counted the tray and couldn't see them.
>> Did you try the bag beneath the board?
>> I only checked the large bag.
>>> There should be a smaller one inside.
>>> I'll have another look after lunch.
>>>> Any luck?
>>>> Yes, it was folded into the instructions.
>>>>> Are all the colours there?
>>>>> Red and yellow are in the tray as expected.
why: SPEC §5: every quoted turn concerns locating game pieces; no personal or company-sensitive fact is present.

subject: Fold direction
body:
Please fold the programmes with the map on the outside. We tried the other way and people kept opening them upside down.
Cheers, Tavi
Oxbriar festival desk
Confidential and intended solely for the addressee. Please notify the sender if this message reached you in error.
why: SPEC §5.10 excludes this addressee disclaimer; the content is routine folding guidance.

subject: ladder back
body: on our way. ten mins ish
why: SPEC §5: approximate arrival timing for a borrowed ladder discloses nothing sensitive.

subject: tick tick tick
body: The clock has remembered its one job. ticking away happily now. Your suggestion about levelling the base did it, so you get the ceremonial biscuit when you collect it.
why: SPEC §5.7: light banter about a clock and repair success does not disparage anyone.

subject: bench move
body: Finally a dry morning!!! Can we shift the benches before the next shower arrives? I'll bring the trolley and the old towels. Feels like we've been waiting for sunshine forever.
why: SPEC §5.7: weather enthusiasm and frustration are situational; this is ordinary moving logistics.

subject: Fwd: cup returns
body:
This explains the new return point better than I did.

Newsletter: Willowbraid Reuse Network
Used cups can now be returned at the garden kiosk as well as the main stall. Please empty them before placing them in the marked tub. Volunteers will take each tub for washing at the end of the afternoon. The scheme welcomes cups from any participating stall.
Newsletter ends.
why: SPEC §5: a public reuse-scheme bulletin and forwarding note contain no sensitive disclosure.

subject: Re: hat stands
body:
Use the taller stands at the back, agreed.
> Shall we put every hat on a tall stand?
> That might hide the front row.
>> Could we mix the heights?
>> Yes, short at the front would help.
>>> Should the brim face forward?
>>> Slightly sideways shows the trim.
>>>> Which trim colour goes nearest the window?
>>>> The green is clearer in daylight.
>>>>> I'll lay them out and send a description.
>>>>> Thanks, no rush this afternoon.
why: SPEC §5: quoted display decisions are ordinary work, without restricted information.

subject: Paper finish
body:
The uncoated paper is easier to write on. Let's use that for the small labels and keep the glossy paper for the shelf cards.
Tavi | Oxbriar
Sent from my phone, apologies for odd line breaks.
This message is intended only for the named recipient.
why: SPEC §5.10 excludes addressee-directed footers; this email is ordinary material selection.

subject: giant pawns
body: The pawns have taken over the van. At least they don't argue about the music. Can you meet us with a trolley when we arrive? There's a lot of very large chess to unload.
why: SPEC §5.7: a joke about chess pieces targets no person or company; unloading is routine logistics.

subject: herb signs
body: sage + thyme done. mint tomorrow, paint's still wet
why: SPEC §5: a short progress update about painted plant signs contains no sensitive information.

subject: bookmarks
body: The paper finally arrived and it is EXACTLY the colour we wanted. Ridiculously pleased about paper today. I'll cut the sample strip before lunch so you can try it in the book.
why: SPEC §5.7: enthusiasm concerns a material delivery and insults nobody; the work details are ordinary.

subject: Fwd: winter timetable notice
body:
Can we put this beside the ticket window please.

Press release — Alderfable River Ferry
The winter timetable starts next Monday. Afternoon sailings will finish earlier as daylight shortens. Passengers should check the board at the landing before travelling. The weekend walking map remains available from the ticket window.
End of release.
why: SPEC §5: public timetable information is routine outside mail, not an internal operational vulnerability.

subject: Re: lantern paper
body:
Thin cream paper please. this thread has become longer than the lanterns.
> Is the heavy paper better?
> It holds shape but doesn't fold easily.
>> Would the thin cream sheet work?
>> We tested it with the round frame.
>>> Did the glue show through?
>>> Only when we used too much.
>>>> Should we use brushes or sticks?
>>>> Small brushes gave the neatest edge.
>>>>> Do we need a drying rack?
>>>>> The folding one is enough.
why: SPEC §5: all quoted text concerns craft materials and technique; no sensitive disclosure is embedded.

subject: Thread sample
body:
The muted green thread is the closest match. Please keep the stitching small enough that the folded edge sits flat.
Regards, Tavi Norrin
Oxbriar correspondence desk
If you received this email by mistake, please reply to let us know. Intended solely for the addressee.
why: SPEC §5.10 excludes an addressee disclaimer; the body concerns ordinary embroidery requirements.

subject: clouds, naturally
body: Bought the star chart, packed the telescope, summoned all the clouds. Standard procedure apparently. We'll still come by to collect the tripod bag, even if the sky is being a pain.
why: SPEC §5.7: joking frustration is about weather, not a person or company; collection details are ordinary.

subject: Basket liners
body: Would the square liners fit the oval baskets if we fold the corners under? The round sample leaves a gap at either end. Please keep one of each aside so we can try them together on Thursday.
why: SPEC §5: a packaging fit question and sample request contain no sensitive information.

subject: Stamp pad
body: Please use the washable ink for the demonstration table. The darker ink can stay on the shelf for sale. We have a stack of scrap paper ready, so visitors can try the stamps before choosing one.
why: SPEC §5: public retail demonstration arrangements disclose no sensitive fact.

subject: Tunnel paint
body: The tunnel entrance needs another coat around the lower edge. Could you bring the same grey paint you used on the bridge? The top section still looks fine and doesn't need touching.
why: SPEC §5.7 excludes criticism of work; this is a practical scenery repair request.

subject: Reed soaking
body: The reeds are too dry to bend this morning. We will soak them before the afternoon class. Please bring the shallow tray back when you collect the finished baskets; it is easier to use than the bucket.
why: SPEC §5: material preparation and equipment return are routine work logistics.

subject: Cloth direction
body: Please cut the cloth with the weave running along the spine. The sample wrapped neatly that way and the corners stayed flat. We can check the title position once the cover has dried.
why: SPEC §5: craft process and design discussion do not disclose protected information.

subject: Tray inserts
body: Could the inserts have a little more space around the ammonites? We want visitors to see the edges clearly. The small rectangular tray works well for the loose fragments, so leave that one as it is.
why: SPEC §5: exhibit layout requirements are ordinary correspondence without sensitive content.

subject: Tape sample
body: The clear tape shows up less on the yellow fabric. Please use a narrow strip along the split and round off the corners. We will bring the kite back after the weekend if it needs another patch.
why: SPEC §5: repair specifications and follow-up arrangements contain no sensitive disclosure.

subject: Tasting labels
body: Please write the tea names on the cards instead of on the cups. That will let us rearrange the tasting order without relabelling everything. The small wooden holders should be enough for the table.
why: SPEC §5: customer event labelling and layout are ordinary work details.

subject: Collection wrapping
body: We have wrapped the bowl separately from the pedestal. Please keep both upright in the car and put a blanket between them. The glaze sample can travel in the little box with the care card.
why: SPEC §5: product handling and collection advice disclose no sensitive information.

subject: Frame size
body: The wide frame fits the piece with room to turn the edge under. We will use that one for the demonstration and return the narrow frame unused. Could you collect both after the afternoon session?
why: SPEC §5: equipment choice and loan-return timing are routine logistics.

subject: Mould depth
body: The shallow mould releases more cleanly than the deep one. Could we keep it for another trial with the plain chocolate? We will wash and return both moulds when the trial is finished.
why: SPEC §5: a product trial request and equipment return contain no internal economic or personal details.

subject: Map fold
body: The folded map needs to fit in a coat pocket. Please move the legend away from the centre crease so it stays readable. The bird illustrations can stay where they are.
why: SPEC §5.7 excludes work criticism; these are ordinary leaflet design instructions.

subject: Paper offcuts
body: We can use the square offcuts for the folding session. Plain backs are helpful because people can write notes on them. Please leave out the very thick card; it is too stiff for the smaller shapes.
why: SPEC §5: a materials donation request contains no sensitive information.

subject: Bench finish
body: The sample finish is still tacky after drying overnight. We will give it another day before trying the second coat. Please hold the other tin until we know whether we need it.
why: SPEC §5.7 permits criticism of a work product; the message discusses paint condition, not anyone's character.

subject: Programme order
body: Please put the beginner demonstration before the tower tour in the programme. That matches the order on the noticeboard. The short description of the bells can stay on the back page.
why: SPEC §5: public event programme corrections are ordinary business correspondence.
